text:
Anya: quick dump — ran A100 vs H100 microbench (mistral-13b) across us-east1 + europe-west1 with simulated KV cache hit rates (75% vs 0%). goal: prefill+decode p50/p95, tokens/sec, and $/1M tokens including amortized GPU cost + infra. attaching CSV snippet below.

Mike: nice, top-line numbers?

Anya: H100 wins latency (p50 decode ~18ms vs 22ms on A100) and higher tokens/sec, but A100 still shows lower $/1M at our current batching due to better price per card in us-east1. europe-west1 has higher egress/costs so numbers flip.

Jordan: can you paste the actual rows? especially curious about cache-hit vs miss delta.

Anya: pasted:
```
model,region,gpu,cache_hit,p50_prefill_ms,p95_prefill_ms,p50_decode_ms,p95_decode_ms,tokens_per_sec,$/1M_tokens
mistral-13b,us-east1,H100,75,120,260,18,48,2900,$28.40
mistral-13b,us-east1,A100,75,150,330,22,64,2450,$24.90
mistral-13b,us-east1,H100,0,220,480,30,110,1300,$62.10
mistral-13b,us-east1,A100,0,270,610,36,140,1100,$75.40
mistral-13b,europe-west1,H100,75,140,300,21,56,2600,$35.20
mistral-13b,europe-west1,A100,75,170,360,26,70,2250,$31.10
```

Dalia: wow cache hit 75% halves cost in us-east1 on H100. what kernel choices did you force? GEMM backend / nostride?

Anya: used runtime defaults + forced int8x4 quantization path for the quant runs (these rows are FP16 baseline). For this run kernel=auto. I also did a small sweep with `--kernel=nvfuser` and `--kernel=te` — nvfuser slightly better on H100 for prefill, TE wins for small-batch decode on A100.

Jordan: did you test small-batch (1-2) cold starts? that matters for PLG tail.

Anya: yes, coldstart single-request prefills are in the 200-400ms range depending on cache. p95 decode spikes when cache miss + cold kv allocation. We added a cache-warmup microbatcher which recovers ~30% of p95.

Mike: what's the dollar calc? how is $/1M computed?

Anya: short: amortized GPU hourly price + infra markup + network egress per-region, normalized to tokens/sec profile for steady-state. formula in run notes: `cost_per_hour / (tokens_per_sec * 3600) * 1e6`. used reserved pricing for A100, on-demand for H100 for conservative estimate.

Dalia: any quantized results? int8x4 vs int4 quality/latency?

Anya: quick summary: int8x4 gives ~1.8-2x tokens/sec uplift with no discernible regression on our eval set (held prompt set). int4 (experimental) gives extra perf but ~3-5% drop on perplexity / some hallucination cases. we flagged int4 for follow-up evals.

BenchBot: run finished, artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-bench/mistral-13b/2470012345-artifacts.tar.gz (logs, traces, perf-profiles, kernel-choices.json) :white_check_mark:

Jordan: can you also push the per-route latency heatmap to the dashboard? would help ops plan SLOs per region.

Anya: will do. next steps: 1) run H100 reserved pricing sim, 2) widen quant eval to larger prompt set, 3) validate nvfuser vs te across more seeds. posting full run notes + reproducer in thread.

Mike: great — add estimated impact on $/1M if we switched to H100 reserved for 12mo. might change the go/no-go for Dedicated SKU.

Dalia: leaving a note to include safety evals for int4 before any rollout.

Anya: ack. I'll tag you when int4 evals land.
